rows.title: Remember identical answers
rows.desc: When the same request with temperature 0 comes again, the saved answer is returned at once instead of being computed again. Requests with a temperature above 0, with images, tools or streaming never use it.

rows.title: Memory for saved answers
rows.desc: The cache never grows beyond this size; the oldest answers go first.

rows.title: Keep answers for
rows.desc: After this time a saved answer is dropped.

rows.title: Who shares saved answers
rows.desc: “Everyone” shares one cache. “Per key and user” keeps the answers of each API key (and the user field of the request) apart; a request that has neither is not saved. Use it when several people use the server.

rows.title: Share the start of prompts
rows.desc: Requests that begin with the same text (a system prompt, a long document) reuse the work already done for it. Turn it off if people on this server must not share anything.

rows.title: Remember the start of a conversation (Qwen3.5, Mamba, RWKV)
rows.desc: Models with recurrent layers cannot point at old work like other models, so they read the whole conversation again on every message. With this on, the server keeps a copy of the model’s state at the end of each prompt and continues from it when the next prompt starts the same way. Automatic: on. Turn it off to save memory.

rows.title: Memory for those copies
rows.desc: One copy of a 9B model takes about 100 MB. The oldest copy goes first when the limit is reached.

rows.title: Separate this installation
rows.desc: A text that keeps the shared prompt blocks of this server apart from those of another server. Leave it empty unless you run several.

rows.title: When memory runs out
rows.desc: “Recompute” drops the work of a waiting request and does it again later (saves memory). “Move to RAM” keeps it in the main memory (faster to continue, needs RAM).

rows.title: Keep shared prompt blocks on disk
rows.desc: A folder where the work done for long shared prompts (system prompts, documents) is saved, so a restart does not have to redo it. Empty means off. Use a fast disk; the folder is never read from another program.

rows.title: Disk space for them
rows.desc: The oldest blocks are removed when the folder is full.

rows.title: Keep the most recent ones in memory
rows.desc: Blocks that were used lately are kept in the main memory as well; reading them is much faster than reading the disk. They are gone after a restart. 0 means off. Works without the folder above.

rows.title: Send traces to
rows.desc: The address of an OpenTelemetry collector (for example http://127.0.0.1:4318). Nothing is sent while it is empty. Only timings and sizes are sent, never the text of a conversation.

rows.title: Name of this server
rows.desc: How the server is called in the traces.

rows.title: Who may administer
rows.desc: This computer always may. Another computer needs an API key with the Admin right (Settings > Server and API). A key made for chatting never opens these controls.

rows.title: Stop taking new requests
rows.desc: The server finishes what it is doing and answers new requests with “busy”. Used before a restart or an update, so nobody loses an answer. Takes effect at once.
